wikitext: {{AnimeLocationInfobox |name=Arche Valley |image=Arche Valley.png |imagesize=300px |characters=アルケーの谷 |japanese=Arche Valley |region=Kalos |colorscheme=ORAS |epicode=Hoopa — The Mischief Pokémon }} '''Arche Valley''' (Japanese: '''アルケーの谷''' ''Arche Valley'') is an {{pkmn|animated series}}-exclusive location in [[Kalos]] and one of the settings of ''[[M18|Hoopa and the Clash of Ages]]''. It is [[Meray]] and [[Baraz]]'s hometown. It debuted in ''[[Hoopa — The Mischief Pokémon]]''. Inhabitants of Arche Valley have slightly different powers compared to people not from Arche Valley. They strive to become one with nature, and are said to be able to communicate with {{p|Arceus}} and receive power from it. There are ivory statues placed throughout Arche Valley that resemble Arceus's ring and are treasured by the townspeople. One hundred years ago, an inhabitant of Arche Valley called [[Ghris]] managed to stop {{an|Hoopa}} [[List of Pokémon with form differences#Hoopa|Unbound]] from destroying [[Dahara City]]. He then sealed away Hoopa's evil power in the [[Prison Bottle]], causing Hoopa to transform into Hoopa Confined. Afterwards, Hoopa went to live with Ghris in Arche Valley. In ''[[Hoopa — The Mischief Pokémon]]'', it was shown that Ghris's great-grandchildren Baraz and Meray grew up here alongside Hoopa, [[Lucianne]], [[Pit]], and [[Kevie]]. ==In the manga== [[File:Arche Valley M18 manga.png|thumb|200px|Arche Valley in ''{{ma|Hoopa and the Clash of Ages}}'']] ===Movie adaptations=== Arche Valley appeared in ''{{ma|Hoopa and the Clash of Ages}}''. {{sectionstub}} ==Trivia== ===Origin=== {{main|Pokémon world in relation to the real world#In the movies|Pokémon world in relation to the real world → In the movies}} The mountainous terrain of the Arche Valley is modeled after the {{wp|Elphinstone Inlet|Khor ash Sham}} and the {{wp|Hajar Mountains}}Location Scouting Report (Chapter 12: The Fjords of the Middle East) on the Pokémon movie website ([https://web.archive.org/web/20180817102935/http://www.pokemon-movie.jp/pokemovie_ch/?p=1107 archived]) (Japanese) ([https://dogasu.bulbagarden.net/movies/2015_xy_archdjinn_rings_hoopa/xy_archdjinn_rings_hoopa_location_scouting.html English translation by Dogasu]), where the former is an inlet in the {{wp|Musandam Peninsula}} in {{wp|Oman}} commonly described as a {{wp|fjord}} and the latter is one of the highest mountain ranges in the {{wp|Arabian Peninsula}} that is located between the {{wp|United Arab Emirates}} and Oman. The settlement features architecture resembling the traditional {{wp|Islamic architecture|style}} of housing in the Middle East, possibly modeled after the historical district of {{wp|Al Bastakiya}}Location Scouting Report (Chapter 5: To Old Dubai!) on the Pokémon movie website ([https://web.archive.org/web/20180817111342/http://www.pokemon-movie.jp/pokemovie_ch/?p=414 archived]) (Japanese) ([https://dogasu.bulbagarden.net/movies/2015_xy_archdjinn_rings_hoopa/xy_archdjinn_rings_hoopa_location_scouting.html English translation by Dogasu]) in {{wp|Dubai}} with the whitewashed buildings potentially inspired by the {{wp|Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque}}Location Scouting Report (Chapter 2: A Baptism of Heat and the White Mosque) on the Pokémon movie website ([https://web.archive.org/web/20180817112244/http://www.pokemon-movie.jp/pokemovie_ch/?p=211 archived]) (Japanese) ([https://dogasu.bulbagarden.net/movies/2015_xy_archdjinn_rings_hoopa/xy_archdjinn_rings_hoopa_location_scouting.html English translation by Dogasu]) in {{wp|Abu Dhabi}}. ==Names== {| class="roundtable" style="background:#{{colorschemedark|ORAS}}; border:3px solid #{{kalos color dark}}" |- !
